title.value: Tiara Ni Clusters for Electrocatalytic Nitrate Reduction to Ammonia with 97% Faradaic Efficiency.

journal.value: Journal of the American Chemical Society

abstract.value: The electroreduction of nitrate (NO<sub>3</sub><sup>-</sup>) for sustainable ammonia (NH<sub>3</sub>) production has recently emerged as a green process to solve water contamination and produce valuable chemicals. In this study, we developed Ni<sub>6</sub>@CuFe-LDH composites comprising tiara Ni<sub>6</sub>(SC<sub>2</sub>H<sub>4</sub>COOH)<sub>12</sub> (Ni<sub>6</sub>) clusters anchored on the edges of 2D CuFe-LDH (LDH: layered double hydroxides) nanosheets via electrostatic interactions. The Ni<sub>6</sub>@CuFe-LDH catalyst exhibits high electrochemical performance in nitrate reduction reaction (NO<sub>3</sub>RR). Specifically, the Ni<sub>6</sub>@CuFe-LDH gives rise to an excellent faradaic efficiency of ∼97%, significantly surpassing the ∼73% FE of the pristine CuFe-LDH, with the NH<sub>3</sub> productivity (0.91 mmol mg<sup>-1</sup> h<sup>-1</sup>) being similar to that of the CuFe-LDH.
